content.text: Infection of the GI tract associated w/ vomiting & diarrhea
▪︎mechanism: ↓ absorption of electrolytes across intestinal epithelium + ↑ secretion (viral/bact toxins act on Na, K, Cl, Ca channels)
▪︎invasive bact (Shigella, Salmonella, Campylobacter): mucosal inflammation & irritation → bloody diarrhea
▪︎acute diarrhea = Sx ≤2wks; visible blood or mucus = dysentery
▪︎viral: incubation 11-72hrs; person-to-person, fecal-oral, contaminated food/H2O; ⍉preformed toxin; N/V, watery diarrhea, mild abd cramps, myalgia
▪︎rotavirus: nonstructural glycoproteins → Cl secretion; fluid follows Cl → secretory diarrhea
– poultry, unpasteurized milk, untx H2O, new pets, dairy farms
▪︎incubation 1-7d; eggs; wild animals or pets; low-grade fever, abd pain & vomiting may precede diarrhea; MC children & young adults

▪︎abx triggers: FQs, clindamycin, broad cephs & broad PCNs; occasional macrolides, TMP-SMX; rare aminoglycosides, tetracyclines, metro, vanco

6) Listeria monocytogenes – contaminated cheese, produce, meat; grows @ low temps → evades sanitary food controls
▪︎incubation 11-72hrs; raw/undercooked seafood, fecal-oral, contaminated H2O; enterotoxins formed b4 & after colonization (⍉preformed); explosive rice-water diarrhea; vomiting, fever, abd cramps
Vibrio parahaemolyticus – raw/undercooked seafood; MC cause of seafood-assoc diarrheal illness; also assoc w/ wound infections & sepsis
– SWINE; pork, milk, well H2O, chitterlings, tofu; uncommon in US
▪︎incubation 1-5d; also fecal-oral & person-to-person; vomiting precedes diarrhea; MC children & young adults
▪︎incubation 1-4wks; person-to-person; flatus, bloating; MC intestinal parasite in US
▪︎also at risk: impaired immunity, MSM, residential facilities; anal-oral sex
▪︎cyst = only infectious form (stomach acid destroys the trophozoite); cysts → duodenum + jejunum → trophozoites emerge
▪︎chlorination ⍉inactivate cysts → filter (pore <1 µm) or boil water for wilderness or international travel
▪︎incubation 1-11wks; poor sanitation; may mimic appendicitis; gradual onset N/V, mild diarrhea
3) Cryptosporidium parvum – intracellular protozoan; contaminated H2O, foodborne, person-to-person, veterinary, respiratory
▪︎acute diarrhea typically w/in 7–10d of ingesting the oocysts; oocysts release 4 banana-shaped motile sporozoites in the small bowel; more common in immunocompromised (HIV/AIDS)
▪︎food poisoning: S. aureus, B. cereus, C. perfringens, E. coli (hx new or raw/undercooked foods w.in 24hrs)
▪︎S. aureus: 1-6hrs; previously cooked foods (ham, egg salad, potato salad); preformed enterotoxin; N, severe vomiting, diarrhea, mild abd cramping
▪︎B. cereus: 1-6hrs; previously cooked meats, fried rice, vegetables, dried fruits; preformed enterotoxin; abrupt N/V, mild diarrhea
▪︎C. perfringens: 8-24hrs; previously cooked/reheated meats & poultry; preformed enterotoxin; abd cramps, N, minimal vomiting, watery diarrhea
▪︎farm animals → Salmonella; travel to resource-limited countries → traveler's diarrhea or Giardia
▪︎community-acquired dysentery → USU invasive bacteria: Shigella, Campylobacter, Salmonella

▪︎also PCR, microscopy (trophozoites or cysts; flagellated protozoan) – needs multiple stool samples; Ag assays cheaper but ⍉eval other pathogens
▪︎Ag testing = preferred (strains visually indistinguishable on stool analysis)
DX (crypto): PCR = standard of care; EIA; stool microscopy: oocysts 4–6 µm
▪︎stool O&P indications: exposure to contaminated H2O, recent prolonged stay in resource-limited country, protracted diarrhea + daycare exposure, or protracted diarrhea in MSM
▪︎healthy pts: no further testing; comorbidities (age >70, pregnancy, HIV, cardiac dz, IBD, high fever, severe abd pain, >6 unformed stools/24hrs, hypovolemia, hospitalization) → stool cultures
▪︎also → workup (IVF, stool cx, abx): Sx >7d, wt loss, abnl serum lytes, pronounced dehydration
▪︎fecal hemocult: ⍉needed if visible blood in stool; may help when pt can't give good hx of stool nature/consistency
▪︎viral GE: USU resolves w/in 60hrs of Sx onset

▪︎daycare/residential facilities: proper diaper disposal + frequent hand washing

▪︎prevention: proper food prep, frequent hand washing
